what: After someone sends the join form, replace "You can close this page now" with a "Get the free app for <gym>" button (the gym's own app link), so the new member installs the app while they still care
why: The join form is the moment a person is most keen, yet the finished card ends the trip; the app that keeps members coming (the owner site's whole promise) is never offered there
impact_why: Every online join, and every gym-page "Become a member", ends on this card; a member with the app is the retention story we sell
my_view: My view: do it first; one button on a card that already knows the gym, using the same smart app link the posters use. Keep the pay box above it.

what: Tag the "Do you own a gym? Get a free page like this one" link on every gym page with a source (for example ?from=gympage) and count those demo requests in HQ, the way member referrals already are
why: Gym pages are the free growth loop for owners, but the link carries no tag, so a lead that came from another gym's page looks like any other visit and nobody can tell if the loop works
impact_why: Tells him whether the free gym page brings new gyms; costs one word in a link and one value in the lead source
my_view: My view: do it; same pattern as ?from=member, no new screen. Add the ad tags (next idea) in the same change.

what: Keep the ad's name on a lead: when the owner site is opened from an ad link (utm_source and utm_campaign), send those two words with the demo request so HQ shows which ad brought each gym
why: Today the only source a lead carries is "member referral"; once he runs Meta or Google ads for gym owners he cannot tell which ad or poster produced calls, so money goes to the wrong ad
impact_why: Matters the day any paid ad runs; without it every rupee of ads is a guess
my_view: My view: do it before the first paid campaign; read two words from the address, keep them for the tab, send them with the form. No tracking script and no cookie, so the privacy notice needs no change.

what: Add a "Chat on WhatsApp" button next to the call-me forms and in the owner site footer, opening a chat with MettleUp's customer-care number
why: The owner site offers only "we call you" and an email address, while the contact page already lists a customer-care phone; Indian gym owners would rather send a WhatsApp now than wait for a call
impact_why: A visitor who wants an answer now leaves if the only way is to wait; WhatsApp is how this audience asks
my_view: My view: do it, with a plain prefilled line ("Hi, I own a gym and want to know about MettleUp") that the visitor sends themself. It lands on one phone, so mind the cover gap already noted for contact paths.

what: After a call-me request, say when the call will come (for example "today between 10 am and 7 pm, or tomorrow morning") and offer "Open the demo gym while you wait"
why: The thank-you line says only "We will call you soon", so an owner does not know when to keep the phone free and has nothing to do next; tools such as Glofox and PushPress let a visitor book a demo time on the spot (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live)
impact_why: Fewer missed first calls; the demo gym link is already on the page but not at this moment
my_view: My view: do the words and the demo link now; a booked time slot can wait until there are more leads than one person can call.

what: Show proof from real gyms on the owner site: once 3 to 5 gyms agree, their name, city and one line each, and "N of 25 founding places left" next to the founding offer
why: The page argues with studies and made-up demo rows only; no real gym is named, and the founding offer says "first 25 gyms" with no sign how many are left. Gym software sites such as Glofox, Gymdesk and PushPress lead with customer names and quotes (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live)
impact_why: Owners trust other owners in their city more than any claim; a live places-left count turns the offer into a reason to act now
my_view: My view: worth it as soon as the first gyms say yes in writing; never invent a quote. The places-left number must come from the real founding count, not typed by hand.

what: Add a 60-second screen video on the owner site (and as the Play promo video): an owner adds a member, the member logs a set, the dues list fills
why: Today a curious owner must open the demo gym and click around to see it work; many will not. A short video shows the whole loop, phone and desk, in one minute
impact_why: Helps the owners who will not try the demo; one video serves the website, WhatsApp follow-ups and the store
my_view: My view: worth doing once the screens stop changing each week; record from the demo gym only, so no real member appears, and load it only on tap so the page stays light.

what: On a gym's web page, when the owner has switched on the free trial, make the top button "Try free for N days" instead of "Become a member"
why: The join form already offers a free trial when it is on, and the question box even suggests asking "Can I try one day first?", but the page's main button never says a trial exists; listing sites such as ClassPass and Mindbody put the intro offer first (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live)
impact_why: A free try is the easiest yes for a stranger; hiding it behind "Become a member" loses people not ready to pay
my_view: My view: do it when the free trial goes live; the page only needs the trial length the join form already reads.

what: Let the owner paste the gym's Google reviews link once, and show "See our Google reviews" in the Find us box of the gym's web page
why: A stranger choosing a gym checks reviews first; the page has photos, fees and maps but no way to the gym's reviews, so they leave to search Google and may land on a rival
impact_why: Helps gyms with good reviews; no effect for gyms with few
my_view: My view: small win, do it with the next page-editor change; accept only Google's own review links, checked like the maps link, and copy no star numbers onto our page.

what: On the member website, next to "Recommend MettleUp to your gym", add "Send the app to a gym buddy" (a WhatsApp share of the app link)
why: The member site has a loop toward gym owners but none toward other members; training partners are the most likely next users, and apps such as Hevy grow through friends (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live)
impact_why: Cheap extra share path; most sharing will still happen inside the app
my_view: My view: do it only together with the in-app share idea already listed, so the words match; one more WhatsApp link, no new tracking.

what: Put "Free, no ads" into the Play short description, the line most store visitors read
why: The listing says free and no ads only in the last line of the long text; the short line does not, while rival logs such as Strong and Hevy put limits behind a paid plan (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live)
impact_why: The short line decides most installs; free with no ads is our clearest edge over paid rivals
my_view: My view: do it, but promise only what stays true: logging free and no ads. Do not say "everything free" while a paid plan for extras is built.
